title: tsdk: multi-discriminator typegen + Zod/JSON-schema adapters for streaming ergonomics
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Goal: Ship a robust type generation pipeline for the TypeScript SDK that produces both static TypeScript types and runtime validators (Zod & JSON-schema) for structured output contracts, with special handling for streaming responses and discriminated unions. The feature should make it ergonomic for application developers to consume streaming model outputs as strongly typed objects, handle evolving schemas, and recover gracefully on transient stream failures (retries/reconnects) without losing user-level pieces of the stream.

Scope: 1) Extend existing codegen to emit multi-discriminator unions and Zod factories that support incremental parsing. 2) Add a JSON-schema output mode for customers that want schema bundles. 3) Surface streaming helpers in the SDK: a streaming parser that yields fully-validated union instances per chunk, a tolerant mode for schema evolution (soft failures), and reconnect/retry semantics that preserve object boundaries and idempotency. 4) Add CLI flags and SDK config for validator caching, source maps for generated types, and backward-compatible naming for previously generated artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: Typegen emits discriminated union TypeScript types and corresponding Zod factories for a sample prompt set (see examples).
SDK streaming parser yields typed objects for each chunk and runs Zod validation incrementally with <50ms median overhead on typical desktop hardware.
Reconnects on transient stream failures resume at object boundaries when producer supports chunk ids; otherwise SDK falls back to user-configurable conservative mode (replay from last checkpoint).
A --json-schema flag produces a single JSON-schema bundle with $defs for each generated type and a mapping file for type -> schema.
Comprehensive unit tests + integration tests covering schema evolution (added optional fields, discriminator renames) and retry behavior are green in CI.
Docs/examples updated in tsdk/docs/structured-output and a short migration guide for existing Zod helpers.
implementation_plan: Design: finalize multi-discriminator representation and runtime tag resolution rules (edge cases: missing tags, nested discriminators).
Codegen: extend codegen library (codegen/gen-types.ts) to emit: 1) NarrowUnion<T> utility, 2) Zod factories with incremental parsers, 3) JSON-schema emitter with $refs and mapping JSON file.

Runtime: implement StreamingValidator in SDK that: a) buffers chunk payloads to preserve object boundaries, b) applies incremental Zod parsing, c) exposes mode flags (strict | tolerant | conservative).

Retry semantics: implement an idempotency token header for stream sessions, store last-committed chunk id per session, and implement exponential backoff with jitter. Add a connection-level checkpoint protocol (best-effort) to resume streams without duplicates when supported by backend.
CLI/DevDX: add tsdk gen --zod --json-schema --out-dir flags and include source maps for generated .ts -> original schema lines to make debugging easier.
Testing: unit tests for generator output snapshots, fuzz tests for malformed discriminator inputs, e2e test against local runtime that simulates mid-stream disconnects.
Docs: short guide + code examples showing stream consumption patterns (for-await-of, on('object'), backpressure), migration notes for existing helpers.
technical_notes: Discriminators: support both 'inline' and 'composed' styles. Inline: {type: 'x', ...}. Composed: {kind: 'x', metadata: {subtype: 'y'}} with resolver rules specified in generated code comments.

Zod incremental parsing: use zod.parseAsync on buffered chunks, but to reduce overhead we will compile and cache a partial-parser per union variant that only validates changed fields. Cache keyed by schema fingerprint (sha1 of schema JSON).

JSON-schema mode: emit $id for each definition and include a top-level 'mapping.json' that maps exported TS type names to schema $id. This avoids expensive reflection at runtime and supports downstream tooling (ajv, jsonschema).

Streaming reconnection: prefer checkpointing at object-level boundaries. If chunk metadata includes sequence_id and object_id, we can resume from last acked object_id. Otherwise, conservative fallback will request replay from beginning of last chunk and re-validate deduplication client-side using ephemeral dedupe keys.

Performance target: additional validator overhead should be <3% of total latency for generation workloads where tokenization and network dominate; we will measure on MacBook Pro M1 and on our standard CI Linux runner.
Open question: should validators be emitted as both Zod and runtime-lite validators (hand-rolled fast validators) for large bundle customers? This could be an opt-in --fast-validator flag in codegen.
Compatibility: maintain file-level exports to avoid breaking existing imports (export * from './generated'; keep stable index file). Use semver-major if we must rename exported types.
